raw_case_text: Case 4: A 26 year old patient that reported exanthema and arthralgia in the second trimester of gestation. The qPCR was positive for Zika in serum (690 copies/ml) and the PRNT90% was positive for neutralizing antibodies. At 37 weeks of gestation, her baby boy was born by cesarean delivery that presented a cephalic circumference of 36.5 cm.

subjective.chief_complaint: 26-year-old pregnant female in the second trimester of gestation presenting with exanthema and arthralgia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed acute exanthema and joint pain during the second trimester of pregnancy. The pregnancy progressed to 37 weeks of gestation, when she gave birth to a baby boy by cesarean delivery.
subjective.past_medical_history: Second trimester of pregnancy; no prior chronic illnesses documented.

objective.physical_examination: Maternal: Cutaneous exanthema. Neonatal: Male infant delivered at 37 weeks gestation by cesarean section with a cephalic circumference of 36.5 cm.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Maternal second-trimester Zika virus infection confirmed by positive serum qPCR for Zika virus (690 copies/mL) and positive PRNT90% for neutralizing antibodies. Pregnancy resulted in a term cesarean delivery at 37 weeks gestation of a normocephalic male infant (head circumference 36.5 cm).
